memory: Osteoarthritis is probably the trickiest condition to manage. I take acetaminophen as needed for mild pain, but when my joints are really acting up, my doctor prescribed meloxicam 7.5 mg, an anti-inflammatory. I don't take it every day because I don't want to overdo it on NSAIDs, but it definitely helps when my knees and hands are particularly stiff. My doctor also suggested trying glucosamine supplements, but I can't say for sure if they've made a difference.I recently had to adjust my vitamin D intake. My last blood test showed my levels were low at 22 ng/mL(normal is above 30 ng/mL), so now I take vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily. I also take calcium supplements since my last bone density scan showed early signs of osteopenia. My doctor recommended I combine it with vitamin K2 to help with absorption.I also take a daily statin—atorvastatin 10 mg—to help with my cholesterol. My LDL was a little high at 130 mg/dL, and my triglycerides were at 140 mg/dL, so my doctor thought a low-dose statin would help. So far, my cholesterol numbers have been improving, and I haven't had any side effects, which is a relief since some people report muscle aches with statins.For general health, I take a daily multivitamin, omega-3 supplements for heart health, and probiotics to help with digestion. Since my gallbladder was removed a few years ago, I sometimes take digestive enzymes if I eat something heavier. Losing my gallbladder changed the way I digest fatty foods, so I have to be mindful of that.One thing I keep an eye on is potential medication interactions. Since I take both losartan and meloxicam occasionally, my doctor warned me that NSAIDs can sometimes affect kidney function, so I try not to take meloxicam too often. I also make sure to take my thyroid medication separately from my calcium and iron supplements, since they can interfere with absorption.Overall, I think my medication routine is working well for me. It's a lot to keep track of, but I make sure to stay organized with a pill planner and use reminders on my phone. I also try to focus on lifestyle changes, so I don't have to rely on medications alone. My goal is to stay as healthy as possible and avoid unnecessary prescriptions by managing things naturally when I can!
